hook.en: A cricket team, a hospital and a factory all need someone to plan, organise and coordinate. That is management.

objectives.en: Define management and explain effectiveness and efficiency
Explain the nature of management as a science, an art and a profession
Describe the levels and functions of management

narration.en: A cricket team, a hospital and a factory all need someone to plan, organise and coordinate. That is management.

body.en: Management is the process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals effectively and efficiently. Effectiveness means completing the right task and achieving the goal on time; efficiency means doing it with the least cost of resources. Characteristics: goal-oriented, pervasive (needed in all organisations), multidimensional (managing work, people and operations), a continuous process, a group activity, a dynamic function (adapting to the environment) and an intangible force (seen only in its results).

title.en: On the board: levels of management

text.en: Board of directors, CEO, managing director
Set objectives and policies; responsible for the whole
Heads of departments: production, finance, marketing
Interpret policies; organise and coordinate departments
Direct and oversee workers; link with the workforce
Coordination is the essence of management

narration.en: Let us build up levels of management on the board, one step at a time.

text.en: Deciding to enter a new market abroad
Preparing the production department's monthly schedule
Checking that workers on a line follow safety rules
Solving a worker's problem on the shop floor

explanation.en: Top managers decide direction, middle managers turn it into departmental plans, supervisors see it done on the floor.

body.en: Management is a science in that it has a body of systematised knowledge and principles, but they are less exact than in physics because they deal with people (an inexact science). It is an art because it requires personal skill, creativity and practice in applying knowledge. It has some features of a profession (a body of knowledge, formal training, a representative body such as the All India Management Association) but not all: there is no compulsory qualification or licence to manage, and no binding code of conduct. So management is both an art and an inexact science, and not a full profession.

points.en: Not a full profession: no compulsory licence

problem.en: A factory produces its target of 1,000 units a day but wastes much raw material. Is it effective, efficient, both or neither?

steps.en: Effectiveness asks whether the goal is achieved: it meets its target, so it is effective.
Efficiency asks whether resources are used well: wasting material means it is not efficient.
